First release of Schema, a PostgreSQL explorer and read-only query toolkit.

Schema answers questions about a database — what is in it, how the tables
relate, how large they are, what a query returns — without being able to
change it.

## What it does

Twelve commands: `connect`, `databases`, `schemas`, `tables`, `describe`,
`relations`, `indexes`, `sequences`, `query`, `export`, `inspect` and
`config`.

- Catalogue inspection read directly from `pg_catalog`: columns with types,
  defaults, identity and generated attributes and collations; primary key,
  unique, check and foreign-key constraints; indexes with their access
  method, validity and size; sequences with their owning column; comments;
  sizes and planner row estimates, with "not analysed" reported distinctly
  from zero.
- Foreign-key relationships, including composite keys and their referential
  actions, with a Mermaid entity relationship diagram on request.
  Relationships come from declared constraints only — a column named
  `user_id` with nothing behind it is not reported as a reference.
- Read-only queries with positional parameters, bounded by a statement
  timeout, a row limit and an output byte budget, read through a
  server-side cursor. CSV and JSON export.
- Diagnostics that mark anything the connected role may not see as "not
  permitted" rather than printing a zero.
- A versioned JSON report for every command.

## Read-only enforcement

PostgreSQL enforces it, in three layers: read-only session characteristics,
`BEGIN TRANSACTION READ ONLY` for the life of the command, and statement,
lock and idle-in-transaction timeouts. A write fails with SQL state `25006`
whatever the client believes.

On top of that boundary, Schema will only send `SELECT`, `WITH`, `TABLE`,
`VALUES`, `EXPLAIN` and `SHOW`. That allow-list is a capability restriction,
not the boundary: it exists because `COPY … TO '/path'` and
`COPY … FROM PROGRAM` are read-only in the transactional sense and still
touch the server's filesystem.

Use a dedicated read-only role as well. `docs/read-only-role.md` has the
SQL.

## Install

Distribution is GitHub only; this is not published to npm.

```sh
base=https://github.com/sablectl/schema/releases/download/v1.0.0
curl -fsSLO "$base/schema-v1.0.0.tar.gz"
curl -fsSLO "$base/schema-v1.0.0.tar.gz.sha256"
sha256sum -c schema-v1.0.0.tar.gz.sha256
tar -xzf schema-v1.0.0.tar.gz
cd schema-v1.0.0
npm ci --omit=dev
node dist/bin/schema.js --version
```

Verify the checksum before running anything.

## Requirements

Node.js 20.19 or later; CI runs 20.19, 22 and 24 on Linux. PostgreSQL 12 or
later is expected; 17 is what this release was developed and tested
against. One runtime dependency, `pg`.

## Known limitations

macOS and Windows are untested. Row counts in listings are planner
estimates. `EXPLAIN` and `SHOW` cannot use a cursor, so their results are
buffered. Table columns are measured in code points, so East Asian text
aligns imperfectly. No benchmarking has been done, so no performance claims
are made. The full list is in `docs/technical-debt.md`.
